## Final report — fix pushed as Gerrit change 2357 (NOT submitted)

Commit `8662526aefdd` on worktree branch `reb-hashbasis-gateref`, off `origin/main`
`565e1856bc9d`. Plan review PASS / certified against that sha before implementation.

### Test (RED -> GREEN, held out, mutation-checked)

`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_ref_coherence.py::test_attested_claim_gate_refuses_to_certify_when_the_gate_ref_is_unresolvable`

* **RED first, for the right reason.** Failed with
  `{'ok': True, 'reason': 'certified plan-review attestation'}` — the fail-open itself.
* **Anti-vacuity anchors** (all asserted, all passing while the test was RED): a CONTROL
  assertion that the gate DOES block while the ref resolves; that the substitution actually
  fired (`_hash_basis(..., at_current_gate_ref=True) == repo_root`); and that the substituted
  basis genuinely holds the reviewed bytes, so an unguarded comparison necessarily finds no
  drift. It also pins `REBAR_GATE_REF=origin/main`, because the suite default is `HEAD` — under
  which the scenario is not expressible at all. That suite default is why this was invisible.
* **Held out**: extracted to a patch outside the worktree and the file reverted BEFORE the
  implementing subagent was launched; the file was declared off-limits to it. GREEN on
  re-application, against an oracle the implementer never saw.
* **Mutation check** (macOS `sandbox-exec`, writes confined to the worktree + scratch):
  re-seeding the exact root cause (disabling the degraded-basis guard) returned it to
  **RED, rc=1**, with the original `{'ok': True, 'certified'}`. Seed application was verified
  by grep, not assumed. Fix restored and re-confirmed green.
* **Refactoring litmus**: asserts only observable output (`claim_gate_check`'s returned dict) —
  no private names, no source greps.

### Fix

* `manifest.py` — `gate_ref_hash_basis() -> GateRefBasis(path, ref, degraded)`. ADR 0002's
  single boundary is preserved (one implementation, not duplicated into the gate).
  `_hash_basis` delegates and keeps its signature, never-raises contract, working-tree
  fallback and operator WARNING **unchanged** — `test_hash_basis_resolution` and the
  `source=local` back-out test are untouched and green.
* `attest.py` — the scoped drift check refuses a degraded ATTESTED basis, naming the ref it
  could not obtain instead of falsely reporting drifted files. Conditioned on the manifest
  carrying a `verified_at_sha`, so pre-S4b attestations keep the lenient basis they were
  always compared against; without that condition an existing test would have been weakened,
  which was out of scope. The drift block was extracted to `_scoped_code_drift` because the
  guard pushed `compute_validity` over its complexity ceiling — behaviour-preserving
  extraction along an existing seam, per the module-size policy, not a baseline bump.

### Scope & safety

* **Caller sweep** — all five consumers of `compute_validity`'s plan-review arm route through
  the one core: `claim_gate_check` (the intended target: now blocks), `plan_review_status`
  (reports it), `reuse.py` (re-reviews rather than reusing — conservative), `retrigger.py` and
  `bugfix_size_gate` (both bucket `stale-code` as `accepted`, unchanged). No behavioural
  dependency on the old fail-open.
* **Review-bot vote unchanged** — verified end-to-end, not argued:
  `classify_plan_review_attestation` -> `verdict=stale-code`, `bucket=accepted`. No new verdict
  literal; `KNOWN_VERDICTS`/`ACCEPTED_VERDICTS` untouched.
* **Restoration, not creation** — restores the documented fail-closed posture; no new entry
  point, command, or user-visible artifact. **No new dependency** (all added imports are
  internal `rebar.*` already used elsewhere). **No test weakening** — the tests diff is
  +50/-0.

### Siblings (Step 7, both axes)

* **Construct sweep** — swept every `resolve_ref` / snapshot-`acquire` site under
  `src/rebar/llm/` and `src/rebar/_commands/`. **One** other site resolves a ref for a gate
  decision, `transition_close._pin_ref`, and it is **not** a sibling: it already documents two
  deliberate policies and states "The pin must never turn a correctly-reported bad ref into a
  silent fallback", failing early on an explicit ref. It is corroborating evidence for this fix
  rather than another instance. No other silent basis substitution exists.
* **Parity census** — rule: *a gate decision must not be computed against a substituted basis
  without saying so.* CLI (`rebar claim` / `transition`), MCP (`claim_ticket` /
  `transition_ticket`), library (`rebar.claim`) and the automated caller (the review-bot) all
  reach the same `compute_validity` core, so the single-site fix covers every surface. The
  mirror operation — the completion-verifier CLOSE gate — is **N/A**: it never calls
  `_hash_basis` (material-fingerprint based) and its ref pin fails closed. No MISSING slots.

### Replication

The original report reproduces end-to-end and is resolved: the deployed WARNING still fires
(preserved deliberately — it is the operator's signal), and the gate now returns
`{'ok': False, 'verdict': 'stale-code'}` with
`"the gate ref 'origin/main' could not be resolved to a snapshot … refusing to certify against
the working tree"`.

### Gates

`make lint` (incl. the complexity ratchet: `new=0 increased=0`) and `make typecheck`
(684 files) exit zero. Regression suite `tests/unit/plan_review`, `tests/interfaces/lifecycle`,
`test_plan_review_attest_drift.py`, `test_opcert_local_verify_binding.py`,
`test_attestation_invalidation.py` -> **842 passed**.

### Residual risk

* **ACCEPTED — the review-bot's 100%-degraded basis.** Its clone can never resolve `origin/main`,
  so the drift half of `classify_plan_review_attestation` is permanently uninformative there.
  That is by design: the gate asks "was an attested review COMPLETED?", which is why `stale-code`
  is accepted. No change warranted, but it means the review-bot cannot be relied on to notice
  drift.
* **TICKET-WORTHY, not filed pending operator direction — the broad `except Exception`.** The
  guard now makes the degradation safe for the claim gate, but the resolution still cannot
  distinguish "no such ref" from "snapshot materialization failed" (e.g. a failed
  `_ensure_blobs_present` top-up, which is explicitly "BEST-EFFORT and silent on failure").
  Both collapse to one warning. Narrowing the except and distinguishing the two in the reason
  would improve box triage. Flagging rather than filing since it borders on the
  `daa7`/queue-owner's area; say the word and I will file it `discovered_from` this ticket.

### Not closing

Per the AGENTS.md ordering, the ticket stays `in_progress` until change 2357 is
`LLM-Review +1` **and** `Verified +1` and has merged. Its close must carry
`--class=regression --caused-by=72d9-8fbd-3a9e-48a6` (the `caused_by` link is already recorded).
